lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Coffee Roasters | Barista | Metro City, USA | Oct 2025 - Present
- Prepared drinks for the morning rush of about 200 orders and kept the bar stocked.
- Opened the café three days a week and handled the daily cash count.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Migrated 40 department sites to a shared component library, cutting new-page build time from 2 days to half a day.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; my findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybook, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Harbor Coffee Roasters leads the engineering story ahead of the more relevant software roles.
items.because: That order can obscure the candidate’s software direction.

items.says: The experience dates leave a gap from August 2024 to June 2025.
The drink-preparation bullet gives the workload but no service or stock outcome.
The opening and cash-count bullet names recurring duties without saying what they achieved.
The café entry takes space for routine work that does not support the software direction.
items.because: Giving café duties space comparable to software roles can weaken the engineering story.

items.says: The 35% performance figure does not name the metric or comparison basis.
items.because: Without the metric and baseline, the improvement is hard to interpret.

items.says: The claim that lazy-loading the hero image cut LCP is technically incorrect.
items.because: Lazy-loading an immediately visible hero image can delay discovery and worsen LCP.

items.says: Storing input in React state does not prevent cross-site scripting.
items.because: React state does not sanitize input, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML can still render injected markup or scripts.

items.says: The XSS-prevention result has no stated evidence showing how it was verified.
items.because: Without a test, scan, or audit, the prevention is difficult to assess.

items.says: The 9% booking result does not say whether it is a relative lift or a percentage-point change.
The strongest internship bullet is not first.
The pronoun “my” makes the research bullet read as a sentence rather than a résumé phrase.
“Writes” conflicts with the role’s ended dates and the other bullets’ past tense.
items.because: Present tense implies an ongoing responsibility despite the August 2024 end date.

items.says: The search-time figures do not specify what interval was timed.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which part of the search experience the figures measure.

items.says: The live-arrivals bullet does not explain how the data is delivered.
items.because: It shows the feature but not the technical contribution behind it.

items.says: The open-source bullet gives external recognition but no technical or domain method.
The booking-flow bullet gives no outcome.
items.because: “Worked on the frontend” does not show what the work enabled or improved.

items.says: The React and TypeScript wording conflicts with the project’s Vue heading.
items.because: The conflicting technologies leave the project stack unclear.

items.says: The calendar bullet does not clarify whether its tests covered the named edge cases or what they established.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the tests covered overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.

items.says: The strongest Library Room Booking bullet is not first.
The travel-search bullet does not fit the library project and closely echoes the Lumen internship achievement.
items.because: A reader may doubt whether it is a separate achievement or belongs in this project.

items.says: The load-time change lacks a comparison baseline.
items.because: “More than halving” does not identify the starting load time.

items.says: The booking change lacks a comparison basis.
items.because: “About a tenth” does not identify the booking baseline.
